rule.title: Mandatory Five-State Component Anatomy
rule.statement: Every data-displaying component must explicitly implement all 5 UI states: Empty, Loading/Skeleton, Error (with retry), Success, and Interactive (Hover/Active/Disabled).
rule.rationale: Failing to design for empty and error states creates broken, blank interfaces when network calls fail or when new users have no data.
rule.implementation_guidance: Provide dedicated sub-components or branches: if (loading) <Skeleton />; if (error) <ErrorView onRetry={retry} />; if (empty) <EmptyView />.

forbidden.example: docs.map(...) directly with no check for docs.length === 0 or error states, rendering an empty white box.

source.chapter: Chapter 11: UI Systems and Atomic Design
source.evidence_quote: A component design is incomplete until all five states have been designed: ideal state, empty state, loading state, error state, and partial state.
